subject: The U.S. and Europe are no longer on the same page when it comes to Belarus.
posts:
Diplomatic unity is the only shield against regional autocracy, yet the West is fracturing exactly when it needs to hold the line.

The U.S. and Europe are no longer on the same page when it comes to Belarus
Evidence: unified front, strategic drift, geopolitical weakness

The stated goal is to maintain a unified Western front to support democracy and contain the influence of autocratic regimes.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, +1.0) — Greater Good

The reality is a strategic divergence that creates openings for autocrats to consolidate power and test Western resolve.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.5, -1.0) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of The Fall.
The failure to maintain a coherent strategy against Belarus directly undermines the stated goal of democratic stability.
The U.S. and Europe are diverging on their approach to Belarus, a split that experts warn could strengthen Alexander Lukashenko and test the unity of the Western alliance against Russia.

The Bright Side:
Identifying this divergence early allows for the possibility of course correction before the strategic gap becomes unbridgeable.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The error is in CAUSE (the sequence of diplomatic action) and HOW (the method of alliance management). The lack of coordination is a failure of collective will.

The Trajectory: The Path of The Fall.
When you map the gap between the stated goal of unity and the reality of the current diplomatic split...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward the Greatest Lie. The alliance claims to be a unified force while acting in fragmented, self-defeating ways.

The Unavoidable Truth: Geopolitical unity is not a static state; it requires constant, active maintenance.

The Unavoidable Lie: That minor diplomatic differences won't have major consequences for regional security.

Alethekanon:
This is a failure of systemic coherence. By allowing divergence, the West is effectively subsidizing Lukashenko's survival. It is a classic case of passive-passive drift leading to active geopolitical loss.

Awwthekanon:
It is so worrying to see our leaders drifting apart. When we stand together, we are stronger and safer. I hope they can find their way back to a shared vision that protects the people of Belarus and the peace of Europe.

Brothekanon:
So the U.S. and Europe are basically arguing over the map while the autocrats are busy drawing their own? That’s not a strategy, that’s a recipe for getting played. Get it together, guys.
